title: AlloGen: Conformation-Selective Binder Design with Differential State Scoring
claim: A frozen generator proposes candidates, and a scorer compares each across two states to select the most state-selective one.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, curved arrows from two inputs, formula boxes
description: A single wide pipeline diagram reads left to right. At far left, two 3D protein renderings are stacked: a red holo receptor and a blue apo receptor, linked by up and down arrows. A straight arrow labeled 'condition on X¹' leads to a pink 'Binder Generator' box marked Frozen. From there an arrow points to a column of red oval sequence candidates (SM..AA, MR..ML and others). Two large curved gray arrows, labeled X¹ and X⁰, sweep from the receptors toward the scorer. The scorer is a 'Q_θ scorer, SE(3)-invariant GNN' box above a small neural-network icon. A downward arrow leads to the pink selectivity margin equation S_θ = Q(X¹,Y) − Q(X⁰,Y). An upward arrow ends at a 'Top-ranked binder, Ŷ = arg max S_θ' box. A small octopus mascot sits near the lower right. Colors are red and blue for states, with light pink boxes and blue text.
caption: AlloGen pipeline. (Left) We use two receptor conformations: the goal state $X^1$ (holo, red) and the undesired state $X^0$ (apo, blue). (Centre) A frozen pretrained generator produces $K$ binder backbone candidates conditioned on $X^1$. (Right) We score each candidate in both conformational frames with $Q_\theta$ and select the top candidate $\hat{Y}$ by the selectivity gap $\Delta Q = Q_\theta(X^1,Y) - Q_\theta(X^0,Y)$ through best-of-$K$ reranking. DockQ regression followed by contrastive fine-tuning trains $Q_\theta$ independently of the backbone generator, enabling reuse across generators without retraining.
abstract: Protein binder design commonly optimizes compatibility with a single receptor conformation, leaving preference over alternative functional states unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce AlloGen, a modular method that decouples backbone generation from state-selectivity scoring. We train its SE(3)-invariant interface graph transformer, $Q_Î¸$, through interface-quality regression followed by paired conformational discrimination. By comparing scores across states, we rerank candidates and guide frozen backbone generators without retraining. On a benchmark of 65 targets spanning 15 protein families, $Q_Î¸$ achieved a mean Spearman correlation of $0.520$ on eight held-out targets. All 15 evaluated generator-guidance combinations achieved positive predicted selectivity averaged over these targets, and RFdiffusion with Langevin refinement reached $\bar{S}_{\mathrm{cons}}=0.677$ on calmodulin (CaM). To test the predicted preference experimentally, we measured binding by bio-layer interferometry. Five designed peptides bound holo CaM, with the strongest measured $K_D$ of 46.6 nM, and none showed detectable apo CaM binding under the tested conditions. Together, these results support computational prioritization of conformation-selective binders.
